newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-GERMAN PAIR BEAT HOLDERS IN TIE-BREAK.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-GERMAN PAIR BEAT HOLDERS IN TIE-BREAK.

text.p: Germans Mandy Woetzel and Ingo Steuer defeated holders Marina Eltsova and Andrei Bushkov in a tie-break in the pairs short programme at the world figure skating championships on Tuesday.
The 1995 champions turned in a near flawless display that was marred only by being briefly out of synchronisation in a side-by-side sit spin.
Bushkov looked a little shaky landing a triple toe loop for their only mistake and neither pair had a majority of first-place votes from the nine judges.
So it went to a total of first and second-place votes, with the Germans outscoring the Russians 8-6 on the judges' cards.
Woetzel and Steuer have engaged the help of a psychologist recently in a bid to overcome problems left from their time together as lovers.
Better communication has helped them deal with the situation and now they may be ready to collect their first world title after being second in 1993 and again last year.
They warmed up by winning the Champions Series title early this month, where they beat Eltsova and Bushkov.
They will go for this title in Wednesday night's free skating.
"Even if we won the Champions Series and skated against all our main competitors, the world championship is something special," Woetzel said.
Young Russians Elena Berezhnaia and Anton Sikharulidze held third place, their final position at the European championships in January.
Berezhnaia is in her first full season with Sikharulidze as her partner after a serious training accident with her former partner whose skate caught the side of her head in practice early last year.
Following surgery to deal with the injury, she has a long scar on her head but says the accident does not cause her any problems.
When she resumed skating after a three-month break, it was with Sikharulidze as her partner. "He is my boyfriend so he will take care of me," she said during the Europeans.
American pairs held fourth and fifth places. World bronze medallists Jenni Meno and Todd Sand were fourth ahead of Kyoko Ina and Jason Dungjen, who took their U.S. title from them last month.

Russians Oksana Kazakova and Artur Dmitriev would have been higher than sixth after a magnificent routine had Dmitriev, a former world, Olympic and European champion with Natalia Bestemianova, not done only a double toe loop instead of the planned triple, which his partner achieved.
Otherwise they were sensational, but the judges penalised then heavily for technique.
Dmitriev's gaffe earned him a frosty reception from coach Tamara Moskvina after they left the ice.
She kissed Kazakova on both cheeks but her greeting to Dmitriev was decidedly offhand.
"The audience should know that Artur had to jump a triple toe loop and not a double. I am angry," she said.
